title: Log-source coverage
feed: T9.2's evidence for A.8.15 and A.8.16
context: At GlobalConnect Manila the SIEM collects the security logs of the Mission Critical systems and, since November 2026, of the remote-access VPN gateway. LogLens is a brand-neutral simulator that shows the same governance information. All log data is synthetic.
atWork: At work, a junior analyst checks what the SIEM really holds before a logging control is rated: which sources can show what happened and when, how long that evidence is kept, and which systems that must send logs do not.
owner: Your sprint rates A.8.15 and A.8.16 from what the Manila office says about its logging. Before you build their evidence, check the SIEM itself on 30 November 2026. The remote-access VPN gateway began sending its logs this month, under the risk treatment plan: can its sources show last week, 23 to 29 November? How long does the SIEM keep events? And which systems send nothing, and must they? Capture what you find, so I can rely on it without opening the console.
rules: Systems within the SIEM coverage of Section 4 send their security event logs to the Group security monitoring platform. Logs are kept for at least 12 months (365 days); the hot, searchable period may be shorter. System clocks are synchronised to the Group time source, so that events from different systems can be put on one timeline.

For a GRC 101 organisation, SIEM coverage is Mission Critical + internet-facing: every Mission Critical system and every internet-facing system sends its logs. SITL-ADD-16 Section 8.1 lists Manila's Mission Critical assets.
A source counts as covered only when its events arrive at the monitoring platform and an alert would fire on them; a source that has gone silent is not covered.
What that means for a source

A source can show a period only if it was connected before the period began and was reporting through it. A source whose clock is a minute or more out goes on a timeline only with its times corrected by that offset.

views.title: Log sources
views.sub: Every source sending events to LogLens. System is the asset register's. Environment says whether the source is production or test.

views.title: Source health
views.sub: Each source's state. Status is No events when nothing has arrived for 24 hours. Clock offset is how far the source's clock is from LogLens's (+ is ahead). Connected on is when the source began sending. All times UTC.

views.title: Retention and settings
views.sub: How long events are kept and who may delete them, as the SIEM is set today.
rows: Device log retention (logs not sent to the SIEM)
Who can delete a server's logs
08:00 to 17:00 on weekdays, by two analysts

views.title: Asset register extract
views.sub: From Manila's asset register, for this check: the Mission Critical systems and the other systems that serve every office or face the internet. Connected sources counts the LogLens sources sending each system's events.

parts.title: The VPN gateway's production log sources
parts.ask: Find every production log source of the remote-access VPN gateway, and capture exactly those.
parts.where: Log sources. Use two filters together: one for the system, one for the environment. Press Capture evidence, then choose the capture here.

parts.title: Can each one show last week?
parts.ask: For each source you captured, decide whether it can show the VPN gateway's week of 23 to 29 November 2026.
parts.where: Source health gives each source's Status, Last event, Clock offset and Connected on, in UTC. The rules you apply say when a source can be used.
options: Use its events as they are
Use it with its times corrected
It cannot show the whole week

parts.title: How long the SIEM keeps events
parts.ask: Which setting says how long the SIEM keeps events? Search for it and capture that one row.
parts.where: Retention and settings. Type part of the setting's name in Search so that only its row is left.

parts.title: Systems that send nothing
parts.ask: Find every system in the asset register extract that sends no logs to LogLens, and capture exactly those.
parts.where: Asset register extract. Connected sources counts the LogLens sources sending each system's events.

parts.title: Which of them must send logs?
parts.ask: For each system you captured, decide whether SITL-POL-009 Section 4 requires its logs in LogLens.
parts.where: Asset register extract gives Mission Critical and Internet-facing. Section 4's SIEM coverage line is in The rules you apply.
